data.title: Govt 'ready' to justify PM's overseas trips
data.description: <p>The government is prepared to defend Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul's foreign policy and overseas trips with concrete results when parliament holds a no-confidence debate, government spokeswoman Rachada Dhnadirek said on Monday.</p>

data.title: Remote surgery 'successful'
data.description: <p>Thailand has performed its first remote robotic surgery for prostate cancer, with a surgical team in Bangkok operating on a patient about 250 kilometres away in Nakhon Ratchasima.</p>

data.title: Committee to review cases for amnesty
data.description: <p>A special committee will review all political cases from 2005&ndash;2025 under the newly enacted Peaceful Society Promotion Act, Prime Minister's Office Minister Paradorn Prissananantakul said.</p>

data.title: KPI chief faces probe over alleged admissions scam
data.description: <p>House Speaker Sophon Zarum has ordered a fact-finding investigation into allegations that King Prajadhipok's Institute (KPI) secretary-general Issara Sereewatthanawut solicited benefits in exchange for admission to an executive programme.</p>

data.title: Business nominee crackdown widens
data.description: <p>Authorities are widening their crackdown on foreign nominee businesses and "grey capital", going beyond raids and asset seizures to trace ownership structures, financial flows and Thai shareholders.</p>

data.title: FM Sihasak kicks off Africa trip
data.description: <p>Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow begins his first official visit to Africa on Tuesday as Thailand seeks to deepen its ties with Nigeria, Ethiopia and the wider continent.</p>

data.title: Navy to extend border fence
data.description: <p>The Royal Thai Navy (RTN) will extend a border fence along the Thai-Cambodian frontier in Chanthaburi by more than 8km as authorities step up security measures along the disputed border.</p>

data.title: NIA cites 3 factors for attacks
data.description: <p>The National Intelligence Agency (NIA) has identified three possible factors behind a series of attacks at more than 50 locations in the deep South late last week, saying they could be linked to preparations for renewed peace talks and an upcoming military rotation.</p>

data.title: Judges query jail sentences
data.description: <p>The Judicial Administration Commission (JAC) has called for a review of criminal sentence enforcement amid concern that serious offenders are receiving large sentence reductions and reoffending after release.</p>

data.title: Four Thai kidnappers arrested while taking Chinese woman to Myanmar border
data.description: KAMPHAENG PHET: Police arrested four Thai men for allegedly kidnapping a Chinese woman from a hotel in Bangkok and taking her to Mae Sot district of Tak bordering Myanmar.

data.title: M82 to Ban Phaeo to open on Friday
data.description: <p>The 16.4-kilometre Ekachai-Ban Phaeo section of the M82 elevated motorway will open for free 24-hour trial use from 10am on Friday, extending the route in operation from Bang Khun Thian to about 25km.</p>

data.title: Thai passport slips in power ranking
data.description: <p>The Thai passport has slipped eight places to 99th in the world, according to a new report by passportreports.com, down from 91st last year.</p>

data.title: Rare B10 coin sells for B2.5m in first online auction
data.description: Thailand's first electronic rare coin auction on Monday featured a 10-baht circulation coin from 1990 that went under the hammer for 2.5 million baht.

data.title: Police armed attack drill sends temple monks fleeing
data.description: NAKHON RATCHASIMA - Monks and novices fled from a temple in terror and hundreds of children were hurredly evacuated from a kindergarten as police staged an unannounced emergency response drill simulating an armed intruder on Monday.

data.title: Popular waterfall closed by rain
data.description: KANCHANABURI - Kroengkrawia waterfall in Khao Laem National Park has been closed to visitors because of the danger posed by the fast flowing river after persistent rain.

data.title: editing   Staged armed attack drill leaves young monks running
data.description: NAKHON RATCHASIMA - Monks and novices fled from a temple in terror and hundreds of children were hurredly evacuated from a kindergarten as police staged an unannounced emergency response drill simulating an armed intruder on Monday.

data.title: 'Wanted' Swedish suspect arrested in Bangkok, and his friend
data.description: A Swedish suspect wanted for alleged attempted murder, extortion and arson in Sweden was arrested at a condominium in Bangkok on Sunday.

data.title: MP faces gambling host, laundering, transnational crime charges
data.description: The Department of Special Investigation on Monday recommended that public prosecutors arraign Klatham Party MP Chonnaput Naksua on charges of organising illegal online gambling, money laundering, transnational crime and illegal assembly.

data.title: Far South violence continues, but reduced
data.description: Dissidents struck again in the southern border province of Pattani late Sunday night, bombing and burning a municipal office, in the wake of a storm of violence in the far South on Saturday night.

data.title: Malaysians advised to defer non-essential trips to south Thailand
data.description: Malaysians have been strongly advised by their own police to put on hold non-essential visits to southern Thailand as bombings, shootings and arson continue to plague the region.

data.title: Exhausted flood-relief volunteer dies in Nan
data.description: A volunteer relief worker was found dead in his hotel room in flood-devastated Nan province on Monday morning, after working tirelessly to help flood victims in this northern province throughout the last week.

data.title: Contract ready for bridge to Koh Lanta, to open in 3 years
data.description: The contract for a road bridge connecting mainland Krabi with Koh Lanta island will be signed next Monday, with the planned opening in 2029, Transport Minister Phiphat Ratchakitprakarn said.

data.title: EC outlines hurdles in Senate election fraud case
data.description: <p>The Election Commission (EC) can refer alleged fraud cases from the 2024 Senate election to the Supreme Court only when three specific legal conditions are met, EC Secretary-General Sawaeng Boonmee says.</p>

data.title: Clear rules on data centres needed
data.description: <p>The government needs to quickly establish clear standards and operating guidelines for data centres to manage the sector's growing demands on resources and the environment, says Surasak Boonrueang, an associate professor at Thammasat University's Natural Resources and Environmental Law Centre.</p>

data.title: Tourist rescued off Nai Thon beach
data.description: PHUKET: A foreign tourist was rescued at Nai Thon Beach in Phuket after ignoring lifeguards' warnings and entering the sea despite a red flag.

data.title: Tourism hub eyed for state land
data.description: PHANGNGA: The Transport Ministry is exploring a 765-rai development in Takua Thung district, with plans for hotels and wellness centres alongside tourism and service activities.

data.title: Democrats seek witness  protection in exam case
data.description: <p>The Democrat Party will petition the National Anti-Corruption Commission (NACC) on Monday for clear guidelines to protect witnesses in the local government examination fraud case.</p>

data.title: 2nd day of M6 trial sees 15k vehicles
data.description: <p>Traffic on the new section of the M6 motorway rose sharply on its second day of trials, with more than 15,500 vehicles using the route.</p>

data.title: Institute vows legal action in bribery case
data.description: <p>Issara Sereewatthanawut, secretary-general of the King Prajadhipok's Institute, has pledged to take legal action over allegations that payments were sought for admission to its executive training programme.</p>

data.title: Knives seized at late-night gathering
data.description: <p>Police in Nakhon Ratchasima detained 16 youths and arrested three men after breaking up a late-night gathering called to prepare for a street fight.</p>

data.title: Nida poll finds doubts over Anutin govt survival
data.description: <p>Almost 40% of respondents in a recent Nida Poll believe Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul's government will not survive its current challenges, with local government examination fraud cited as its biggest problem.</p>

data.title: Sombat faces sex assault allegations
data.description: <p>Political activist Sombat Boonngamanong is the latest prominent activist to face sexual assault allegations rocking Thailand's pro-democracy movement.</p>

data.title: Army plays down attacks
data.description: <p>A coordinated wave of 51 attacks across Narathiwat, Pattani and Yala may have been launched to discredit state officials and retaliate against a crackdown on illicit trade, Fourth Army Area commander Lt Gen Norathip Phoynok says.</p>
